name: Kaufland Marketplace
description: Kaufland Marketplace (formerly real.de) seller API: orders and their units, shipments, storefront listings, units, tickets and warehouses. HMAC-signed requests — the signature covers the method, URL, body and a timestamp.
instructions:
**Getting credentials**
1. You must already be a Kaufland Marketplace seller. In the **Seller Portal** open **Settings → API keys** and create a key pair.
2. You receive a **Client Key** (public, identifies you) and a **Secret Key** (never sent — it signs the request). Set `KAUFLAND_CLIENT_KEY` and `KAUFLAND_SECRET_KEY`.

**The secret never travels.** Kaufland does not accept a bearer token: every request carries `Shop-Client-Key`, `Shop-Timestamp` and `Shop-Signature`, where the signature is an HMAC-SHA256 over the canonical string

```
<METHOD>\n<FULL URL INCLUDING QUERY>\n<BODY>\n<UNIX TIMESTAMP>\n
```

keyed with the secret. AnythingMCP computes it per request and sends the timestamp it used, so the server can recompute the same string.

**A signature is only valid for a few minutes.** Kaufland rejects a request whose timestamp has drifted, which means a 401 here can be a clock problem rather than a key problem. If every call fails and the keys are definitely right, check the host's time.

**Storefronts are per country.** Kaufland runs `de`, `cz`, `sk`, `pl` and `at` storefronts and most endpoints take a `storefront` parameter. Omitting it gives you the seller's default, which is rarely what a report about one market wants.

**Orders page with offset and limit**, and `ts_created_from` / `ts_created_to` bound the window — both ISO 8601. Ask for the window you mean; the default is short.

**Order units are where the money is.** An order carries `order_units`, each with its own status, price and fulfilment state. A part-cancelled order is normal, so a revenue figure should sum the units that were actually fulfilled rather than the order total.

**Cloud reachability**: sellerapi.kaufland.com is public with a valid certificate.

tools.name: kaufland_list_warehouses
tools.description: List the seller's warehouses with their id, name and address. No parameters — the lightest call, and the quickest proof that the key pair and the host clock both line up.

tools.name: kaufland_list_orders
tools.description: List orders in a time window with their buyer, storefront, totals and status. Bound the window explicitly: the default is short and a report that silently used it will understate the period.

storefront.description: Storefront to query: de, cz, sk, pl or at.

embedded.description: Related objects to expand inline, e.g. order_units,order_invoices.

tools.name: kaufland_get_order
tools.description: Read one order in full: the buyer, the delivery address, the payment and every order unit with its own price, status and fulfilment state.

embedded.description: Related objects to expand, e.g. order_units.

tools.name: kaufland_list_order_units
tools.description: List individual order units — the level Kaufland actually fulfils, cancels and pays out at. A part-cancelled order is normal, so revenue should be summed here rather than from the order total.

storefront.description: Storefront to query: de, cz, sk, pl or at.

status.description: Unit status, e.g. open, sent, cancelled, returned.

tools.name: kaufland_list_units
tools.description: List the seller's units (offers) with their EAN, condition, price, stock and the storefront each is listed on.

storefront.description: Storefront to query: de, cz, sk, pl or at.

tools.name: kaufland_list_shipments
tools.description: List reported shipments with their carrier, tracking number and the order units they cover — the answer to whether something has actually gone out.

tools.name: kaufland_list_tickets
tools.description: List customer service tickets with their subject, status and the order they relate to — where a buyer complaint shows up before it becomes a rating.

tools.name: kaufland_list_storefronts
tools.description: List the storefronts this seller is active on, with the currency and locale of each. Use it to find the storefront code the other tools need.
